items.statement: Let $c>0$. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open set that is star-shaped with respect to a point $a\in\Omega$ ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with at least two elements ([[def-interval]]). Fix an integer $k\ge2$ and let $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be fields of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-em-fields]]) satisfying the two source-free Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on $\Omega\times I$ in their pointwise form $$\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,$$ with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Then there are a scalar potential $\varphi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly and a vector potential $A:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^k$ jointly ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]) with $$B=\operatorname{curl}A,\qquad E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$ If $E$ and $B$ are of class $C^\infty$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$, then $\varphi$ and $A$ may be chosen of class $C^\infty$ jointly. Conversely, if $\varphi$ and $A$ are of class $C^\infty$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ and $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\operatorname{curl}A$ are their field pair, then $(E,B)$ satisfies $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ on $\Omega\times I$. The theorem asserts existence on the stated star-shaped domain only: it claims no global potential on a general open $\Omega$, no boundary or decay condition on the potentials, and no uniqueness; potentials are auxiliary objects of the framework and not claimed to be observable.

items.physical_scope: The fields and potentials of the classical vacuum electromagnetic framework of [[def-em-fields]], [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]] on a single inertial laboratory region over a star-shaped spatial region. The only physical hypothesis used is the pair of source-free Maxwell equations (absence of magnetic charge and Faraday's law) as adopted in the postulate; no source equation, no regularity beyond the stated joint class, and no assertion that the potentials are observable are included. The star-shaped hypothesis is a genuine restriction on the spatial region, and the companion examples exhibit a divergence-free field on a non-star-shaped region with no global vector potential.

items.title: Potential representations, gauge transformations and gauge equivalence of the framework's fields
items.design_state: explicit-definition-contract; class bookkeeping and the smooth group action are stated exactly; reachability is excluded by contract
items.statement: Let $c>0$, let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ with its restricted inertial chart be that of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], let fields and units be those of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let the potential-pair vocabulary (scalar-vector pair, field pair $E(\varphi,A),B(\varphi,A)$, Lorenz divergence $G$, Lorenz gauge, gauge transform $T_\chi$ and wave expression $W$) be that of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]] on that region. (a) [Representations] For a field pair $(E,B)$ of class $C^{k-1}$ on $\Omega\times I$ and an integer $k\ge2$, a **potential representation of class $C^k$** of $(E,B)$ is a pair $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ whose field pair is $(E,B)$, that is, $\varphi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $A:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^k$ jointly ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with $$E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA,\qquad B=\operatorname{curl}A\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I,$$ the derivatives being those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. This definition asserts neither existence (supplied on star-shaped regions under their stated hypotheses by [[pthm-em-spacetime-potentials]]) nor uniqueness of a representation. (b) [Gauge functions and gauge equivalence] A **gauge function** of class $C^m$ ($m\ge2$) on $\Omega\times I$ is a function $\chi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^m$ jointly; its **gauge transformation** acts on a potential pair by $$T_\chi(\varphi,A):=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,\ A+\nabla\chi),$$ the transform of a $C^m$ pair being a potential pair of class $C^{m-1}$. Two pairs are **gauge related** when one is the transform of the other by some gauge function. On pairs and generators of class $C^\infty$, $T_0$ is the identity and $T_{\chi_1}(T_{\chi_2}(\varphi,A))=T_{\chi_1+\chi_2}(\varphi,A)$ for all $C^\infty$ generators $\chi_1,\chi_2$ ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], componentwise); hence gauge relatedness is an equivalence relation on the $C^\infty$ potential pairs. (c) [Conditions] A pair is **in Lorenz gauge** on $\Omega\times I$ when $G=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi=0$ there, and **in Coulomb gauge** in the chosen spatial chart when $\operatorname{div}A=0$ there. These are properties of a pair in the stated conventions. The existence of a gauge function achieving a condition, with or without prescribed initial or boundary data, is a separate PDE conclusion with its own hypotheses and is not part of this definition. (d) [Physical status] The physical content of a representation is its field pair $(E,B)$ of [[def-em-fields]]; the pair $(\varphi,A)$ and the gauge function are auxiliary, their values are convention dependent, and gauge related representations have the same field pair. The scalar potential carries the volt and the vector potential the tesla metre, consistently with [[def-em-si-conventions]]; no value of $\varphi$ or $A$ is by itself an observable or evidence for a field.

items.title: Gauge transformations preserve the field pair: invariance of the electric and magnetic fields
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval with at least two elements ([[def-interval]]), $c>0$, and fix $k\ge2$. Let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ and let $\chi$ be a gauge function of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]], [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]). Then the gauge transform $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,\ A+
abla\chi)$ is a potential pair of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly and its field pair is the field pair of $(\varphi,A)$: $$E(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=E(\varphi,A),\qquad B(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=B(\varphi,A)\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I,$$ the common value being a map $\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly (the field pair of $(\varphi,A)$ in the sense of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]). In particular, gauge related potential representations of a field pair ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]) have equal field pairs: the electric and magnetic fields are gauge invariants of the framework, and no value of $\varphi$, $A$ or $\chi$ is asserted to be observable. The identity uses only the definitions $E=-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B=\operatorname{curl}A$, the vanishing of $\operatorname{curl}
abla\chi$ for the $C^2$ function $\chi$ and the equality of the mixed partials $\partial_t\partial_i\chi=\partial_i\partial_t\chi$; no Maxwell equation, no hypothesis on $\Omega$ beyond openness and no choice principle is used.

items.title: Maxwell's equations in potential form: the Lorenz divergence, the decoupled wave equations and residual generators
items.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; the exact algebraic identities are stated with their pointwise-regularity hypotheses; solvability is left to the reachability theorem
items.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval, $c>0$, and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ ([[def-em-fields]]) and Lorenz divergence and wave operator $$G:=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi,\qquad W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta.$$ Let $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous sources ([[def-em-sources]]). (a) [Exact identities] Independently of any field equation, on $\Omega\times I$ $$\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+\nabla G.$$ Consequently the sourced Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold for $(E,B,\rho,J)$ if and only if $$W\varphi-\partial_tG=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad WA+\nabla G=\mu_0J\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$ (b) [Gauge shift] If $\chi$ is a gauge function of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$, then $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G-W\chi$ on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]), and the transformed pair has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). Hence $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge if and only if $W\chi=G$ on $\Omega\times I$. (c) [Decoupling] For this pair and sources, the pair is in Lorenz gauge and satisfies the two decoupled sourced wave equations $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and $WA=\mu_0J$ if and only if its field pair solves the sourced Maxwell system on $\Omega\times I$ (the source-free pair $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ being automatic for a potential pair). Thus in Lorenz gauge the sourced Maxwell system is exactly a pair of decoupled wave equations, componentwise for $A$. (d) [Residual generators] If $W\chi=0$ then the transform of a pair in Lorenz gauge is again in Lorenz gauge with the same field pair; the Lorenz condition therefore does not determine the potential pair. (e) [Scope] The identities and equivalences are properties of a given potential representation of class $C^2$; they assert no existence of a generator with $W\chi=G$ (or with prescribed data), which is the subject of the gauge-reachability theorem on this page, and they impose no boundary, decay or initial condition. A pair of class $C^1$ defines $E,B$ but need not have the second derivatives appearing in $W\varphi$, $WA$, $\Delta$ or $\partial_tG$, so $C^2$ is the exact standing regularity here.
items.strategy:
(a) Componentwise expansion using the sum rules for divergence and curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]), the vector identity $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A=
abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A$ for the $C^2$ field $A$ ([[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]]), the definition $\Delta\varphi=\operatorname{div}
abla\varphi$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]) and the equality of mixed partials of the $C^2$ functions $\varphi,A$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]): $\operatorname{div}E=-\Delta\varphi-\partial_t\operatorname{div}A=W\varphi-\partial_tG$, and $\operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=
abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=WA+
abla G$. The two source-free equations hold automatically for a potential pair by [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and [[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]] with the linearity of curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]); hence the equivalence with the sourced system. (b) Direct expansion of $T_\chi$: $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=\operatorname{div}A+\Delta\chi+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi-c^{-2}\partial_t^2\chi=G-W\chi$, using linearity and the $C^2$ mixed-partials identity for $\chi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]); the field part is [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]. (c) is the combination of (a) and (b) with the automatic source-free pair; (d) is (b) with $G=0$ and $W\chi=0$. All statements are pointwise on $\Omega	imes I$; the constants $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ are those of the framework postulates ([[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]). No choice principle, no hypothesis on the shape of $\Omega$ and no solvability of $W\chi=G$ is used.

items.physical_scope: The exact algebraic content of the adopted vacuum Maxwell system in terms of a potential representation of class C^2 on a laboratory region: the sourced Maxwell equations are equivalent to two sourced wave equations plus the Lorenz condition, and gauge generators with W chi = 0 preserve the condition while leaving the fields unchanged. The statement is conditional on joint C^2 regularity of the pair; it asserts no existence of gauge generators meeting any data, makes no empirical claim, and does not identify the potentials with observable quantities.

items.title: Gauge reachability: Lorenz gauge on the all-space slab and Coulomb gauge on a bounded smooth domain, with residual freedom
items.reference: core-conditional-proofs.md#K7 and completed-expansion-arguments.md#W6; bounded-domain branch closed locally with the published elliptic resolvent and higher-order Dirichlet estimates
items.design_state: complete branch argument for the two declared branches; the older global gauge promise on bounded domains with prescribed data is outside the statement, as the design requires
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ in branch (a) and the Axiom of Choice together with $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as declared by its weak-solvability lemmas in branch (b) ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $c>0$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of the framework ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ and Lorenz divergence $G=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$. (a) [All-space slab; Lorenz gauge] Let $t_0<T$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ (the restriction of a $C^\infty$ pair on $\mathbb R^3\times J$ for some open interval $J\supset[t_0,T]$; [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ with $\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$, $\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $W\chi=G$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$; the transformed pair $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$, has the same field pair $(E,B)$, and any two such gauge functions differ by a solution of $W\chi=0$. This is the exact content of [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] read for potential pairs of the framework; its physical content is that every smooth potential representation of a field pair on a slab admits a Lorenz-gauge representative with zero gauge Cauchy data at $t_0$, without changing the fields. (b) [Bounded smooth domain; Coulomb gauge] Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval and let $(\varphi,A)$ be of class $C^\infty$ on a neighbourhood of $\bar\Omega\times\bar I$. Fix a smooth time-independent Dirichlet datum $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$. Then there is a gauge function $\psi$, of class $C^\infty$ on a neighbourhood of $\bar\Omega\times\bar I$, with $\psi(\cdot,t)|_{\partial\Omega}=g$ for every $t\in I$, such that $$\operatorname{div}(A+\nabla\psi)(\cdot,t)=0\qquad\text{on }\Omega\text{ for every }t\in I;$$ the transformed pair $T_\psi(\varphi,A)$ is in Coulomb gauge on $\Omega\times I$ and has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). The generator is unique among such generators with datum $g$; if $g=0$, then $\psi$ is the unique generator with zero boundary values. (c) [Residual freedom on star-shaped domains] Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and star-shaped ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let $(\varphi,A)$, $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)$ be two potential pairs of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-interval]]) with the same field pair, both in Lorenz gauge. Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^2$ jointly with $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)=T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ and $W\chi=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. (d) [Scope] Nothing is asserted about gauge functions meeting arbitrary prescribed boundary or initial restrictions: in (a) the gauge function has zero Cauchy data at $t_0$ and no spatial boundary condition or decay, and $\Omega$ is all of $\mathbb R^3$; in (b) the datum is the fixed time-independent Dirichlet datum $g$ and the Neumann variant with its own compatibility condition for every $t$ is not claimed; the older promise of a global Lorenz gauge on a bounded domain with prescribed boundary data is explicitly outside this result. The Coulomb-gauge statement concerns the spatial divergence in the chosen inertial chart, and the instantaneous appearance of the Coulomb potential is a property of the representation, not a signal: only the field pair $(E,B)$ is physical content ([[def-em-fields]]).

(a) is [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] with its hypotheses and countable choice carried verbatim; the pair of the framework enters only through the vocabulary, so nothing is reproved. (b) Fix $g$ and let $h\in C^\infty( ar\Omega)$ be the solution of $-\varepsilon_0\Delta h=0$ in $\Omega$ with $h|_{\partial\Omega}=g$ ([[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](a) with $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0 I$ and $ho=0$). items.title: Topological obstructions to global potentials: a curl-free loop field and a divergence-free sphere-flux field
items.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; the vector obstruction is sharpened from C^2 to C^1 potentials by patch Stokes plus internal edge cancellation
items.statement: (a) [Scalar obstruction] On $U_1:=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{(0,0,z):z\in\mathbb R\}$ the field $F(x,y,z):=(-y,x,0)/(x^2+y^2)$ is of class $C^\infty$, satisfies $\operatorname{curl}F=0$ on $U_1$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]), and is not the gradient of any $C^2$ function on $U_1$: its circulation around the positively oriented unit circle $\gamma(t)=(\cos t,\sin t,0)$, $t\in[0,2\pi]$, equals $2\pi$, since the pullback identity ([[lem-a-vector-line-integral-pulls-back-to-the-parameter-region]], [[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]) gives $F(\gamma(t))\cdot\gamma'(t)=1$ by the sine and cosine derivatives and the Pythagorean identity ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]), and $\int_0^{2\pi}1\,dt=2\pi$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]); whereas for a $C^2$ potential $\varphi$ on $U_1$ the gradient theorem gives $\oint_\gamma\nabla\varphi\cdot d\mathbf r=\varphi(\gamma(2\pi))-\varphi(\gamma(0))=0$ ([[thm-gradient-theorem-for-line-integrals]], [[def-closed-and-exact-c1-vector-fields]]). Hence a curl-free $C^\infty$ field on a connected open set need not have a global scalar potential, and the star-shaped hypothesis of [[pthm-em-spacetime-potentials]] cannot be dropped. (b) [Vector obstruction] On $U_2:=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ the field $B(x):=x/\|x\|_2^3$ is of class $C^\infty$ and satisfies $\operatorname{div}B=0$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]), but there is no vector potential $A$ of class $C^1$ on $U_2$ with $\operatorname{curl}A=B$ ([[def-vector-potential-of-a-c1-vector-field]]). To see this, let $\Phi(\phi,\theta):=(\sin\phi\cos\theta,\sin\phi\sin\theta,\cos\phi)$ be the spherical parametrization, a regular patch on the rectangle $[0,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$ whose longitude seam and poles lie on the parameter boundary ([[def-admissible-regular-parametrized-surface-patch]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-parametrize-the-unit-circle]], [[thm-sine-cosine-signs-monotonicity-and-ranges]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]]); the flux of $B$ through the unit sphere in this orientation is $\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\pi\langle B(\Phi),(\Phi_\phi\times\Phi_\theta)\rangle\,d\phi\,d\theta=\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\pi\sin\phi\,d\phi\,d\theta=4\pi$, because $\Phi_\phi\times\Phi_\theta=\sin\phi\,\Phi$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]], [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[thm-jordan-fubini-by-sections]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]]). Applying the classical Stokes theorem ([[thm-the-classical-stokes-theorem-for-a-c2-surface-patch]]) to the two closed rectangular hemispheres $[0,\pi/2]\times[0,2\pi]$ and $[\pi/2,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$ ([[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]], [[def-type-i-type-ii-and-elementary-green-regions]], [[def-positive-orientation-for-elementary-region-boundaries]]) expresses the flux of $\operatorname{curl}A=B$ over each hemisphere as the circulation of $A$ around its induced boundary chain; in each hemisphere the two image meridian edges have the same image traversed in opposite directions and their integrals cancel ([[thm-line-integrals-under-reversal-and-concatenation]]), while the polar edge is degenerate, so the two circulations are the integral of $A$ over the equator and its reverse, cancelling each other; adding the two identities therefore gives $4\pi=0$, a contradiction. Consequently a divergence-free $C^\infty$ field on an open subset of $\mathbb R^3$ need not have a globally defined vector potential, and the star-shaped hypothesis of the potential theorem is substantive for the vector potential as well. (c) [The punctured space is simply connected] $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ is simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]): it is path connected ([[def-path-connected]], [[cor-euclidean-spheres-are-path-connected]]), and every loop at every basepoint is null-homotopic. Indeed, for a basepoint $x_0$ with $\rho:=\|x_0\|_2>0$ the linear scaling $L(x):=x/\rho$ and its inverse are continuous bijections of $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ ([[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]], [[thm-bounded-linear-operator-equivalences]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]); a loop $\gamma$ at $x_0$ is null-homotopic if and only if $L\circ\gamma$ is, so it suffices to treat basepoints on the unit sphere. For $x_1$ on the unit sphere the radial homotopy $H(x,t)=((1-t)+t/\|x\|_2)x$ is continuous, fixes the unit sphere pointwise and deforms a loop at $x_1$ to a loop in the unit sphere ([[thm-radial-straight-line-map-on-punctured-rn]], [[lem-radial-normalisation-is-continuous]]); the loop in the unit sphere is null-homotopic rel basepoint there because $S^2$ is simply connected ([[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]]), and composing that homotopy with the inclusion gives a null-homotopy in $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ ([[def-homotopy-relative-and-path-homotopy]], [[def-based-loops-and-fundamental-group]]). Thus the domain of the vector obstruction, unlike the domain of the scalar obstruction, admits no winding invariant, and simple connectivity of the domain is not by itself sufficient for the existence of a vector potential. (d) [Scope] The two obstructions have different characters: (a) is detected by the circulation of a closed loop, (b) by the flux through a closed surface. The fields displayed are smooth mathematical witnesses on the punctured open sets; the framework's postulate [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] excludes magnetic charge, and no physical source, physical singularity or empirical claim is attached to them.
items.strategy: (a) Differentiate the components of $F$ by the quotient rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) to get $\operatorname{curl}F=0$; parametrize the unit circle, use the pullback identity for vector line integrals and the sine/cosine derivative and Pythagorean identities to get $F(\gamma(t))\cdot\gamma'(t)=1$, and evaluate $\int_0^{2\pi}1\,dt=2\pi$ by the fundamental theorem ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]). The gradient theorem for a $C^2$ potential gives zero circulation around the closed curve $\gamma$, so $F$ is not a gradient ([[thm-gradient-theorem-for-line-integrals]], [[def-closed-and-exact-c1-vector-fields]]). (b) Compute $\operatorname{div}B=\sum_i\partial_i(x_i\|x\|_2^{-3})=3\|x\|_2^{-3}-3\|x\|_2^{-5}\sum_ix_i^2=0$ by the chain and product rules ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]). For the flux, differentiate $\Phi$ to get $\Phi_\phi\times\Phi_\theta=\sin\phi\,\Phi$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]]); since $B(\Phi)=\Phi$ on the unit sphere, the integrand is $\sin\phi$, and Fubini with the fundamental theorem evaluate the double integral as $4\pi$ ([[thm-jordan-fubini-by-sections]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]). Suppose $A$ is $C^1$ on the open set $U_2$ with $\operatorname{curl}A=B$. Each hemisphere rectangle is a finite elementary Green region with its positive boundary chain and the spherical parametrization restricted to it is a $C^2$ regular patch whose image lies in $U_2$, so the classical Stokes theorem applies to each ([[def-type-i-type-ii-and-elementary-green-regions]], [[def-positive-orientation-for-elementary-region-boundaries]], [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]], [[thm-the-classical-stokes-theorem-for-a-c2-surface-patch]]). In each hemisphere the induced boundary chain has four entries: one equator arc, two meridian arcs with the same image and opposite orientations, and one degenerate polar arc; the two meridian integrals cancel by reversal ([[thm-line-integrals-under-reversal-and-concatenation]]) and the degenerate one is zero. Hence the north circulation is the equator integral and the south circulation is its reverse, so their sum is zero; summing the two Stokes identities gives zero for the total flux of $B$ over the sphere, contradicting $4\pi\ne0$, and no such $A$ exists. (c) For the basepoint reduction, $L$ and $L^{-1}$ are linear maps of $\mathbb R^3$, hence bounded and continuous on the finite-dimensional space ([[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]], [[thm-bounded-linear-operator-equivalences]]), so a null-homotopy of $L\circ\gamma$ composed with $L^{-1}$ is one of $\gamma$; for a basepoint on the unit sphere, $H$ is the continuous radial homotopy of [[thm-radial-straight-line-map-on-punctured-rn]] fixing the unit sphere, so it deforms the loop to a loop in $S^2$ rel basepoint ([[def-homotopy-relative-and-path-homotopy]], [[def-based-loops-and-fundamental-group]]), which is null-homotopic rel basepoint by simple connectivity of $S^2$ ([[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]]); composing with the inclusion and concatenating gives the required null-homotopy in $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$. Path connectedness of $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ is seen by routing through the unit sphere ([[cor-euclidean-spheres-are-path-connected]], [[def-path-connected]]). (d) is the comparison of the two mechanisms: circulation versus flux. All suppliers are published items used at their stated hypotheses; no choice principle is used.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval ([[def-interval]]), and let $\chi:\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R$ be of class $C^2$ jointly ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Then the pair $$(\varphi,A):=T_\chi(0,0)=(-\partial_t\chi,\ 
abla\chi)$$ is a potential pair of class $C^1$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ whose field pair is the zero field pair: $$E(\varphi,A)=-
abla(-\partial_t\chi)-\partial_t(
abla\chi)=0,\qquad B(\varphi,A)=\operatorname{curl}
abla\chi=0\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I$$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]), the first identity by the equality of the mixed partials $
abla\partial_t\chi=\partial_t
abla\chi$ of the $C^2$ function $\chi$ and the second by [[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]]. Explicit instance: for $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $ eta\in\mathbb R$ and $\chi(x,t)=a\cdot x- eta t$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$, the pair is the nonzero constant pair $(\varphi,A)=( eta,a)$, with $E=-

Thus the map from potential pairs to field pairs of [[def-em-fields]] is not injective: nonzero potentials may represent the zero field pair (pure-gauge fields), and no nonzero value of $\varphi$ or $A$ alone is evidence for a nonzero field, consistently with [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]] and [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]. The field pair of the zero pair is $(0,0)$; by [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]] the transformed pair has the same field pair, which is $(0,0)$. The explicit formulas are then recomputed directly: with $\chi(x,t)=a\cdot x-\beta t$ one has $\partial_t\chi=-\beta$ and $\nabla\chi=a$, so $(\varphi,A)=(\beta,a)$; the fields of a constant pair vanish because every partial derivative of a constant is zero ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). items.title: A homogeneous-wave gauge generator changes Lorenz potentials without changing their fields
items.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; explicit real cosinusoidal generator with |k| = omega/c
items.statement: Let $c>0$, let $k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, $\omega:=c|k|$, and let $$\chi(x,t):=\cos(k\cdot x-\omega t),$$ the real part of the complex plane wave $e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)}$ of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] with wave vector $k$ and frequency $\omega=c|k|$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then $\chi$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ and $W\chi=0$, where $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ ([[def-wave-equation-cauchy-data-and-wave-speed]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]); indeed $\partial_t^2\chi=-\omega^2\chi$, $\Delta\chi=-|k|^2\chi$ and $\omega^2=c^2|k|^2$, so $W\chi=c^{-2}(-c^2|k|^2\chi)+|k|^2\chi=0$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). Consequently, for every potential pair $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^2$ jointly on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]), the gauge-transformed pair satisfies $$G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G(\varphi,A)\qquad\text{and}\qquad E(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=E(\varphi,A),\quad B(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=B(\varphi,A)$$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ ([[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]], [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]], [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]); in particular, if $(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge then $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge with the same field pair. Explicitly $\partial_t\chi=\omega\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$ and $\nabla\chi=-k\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$, so $\varphi'=\varphi-\omega\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$, $A'=A-k\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$; the zero pair is in Lorenz gauge and its transform $(-\omega\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t),\ -k\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t))$ is a nonzero pair that remains in Lorenz gauge and still represents the zero field pair. Thus the Lorenz condition does not determine the potential pair. The example is the residual generator $W\chi=0$ of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]] on the free-space branch; on a bounded domain with prescribed gauge boundary data the admissible generators are restricted, and no such data-dependent claim is made here.

Substitute $\omega^2=c^2|k|^2$ to get $W\chi=0$. Then use the gauge-shift identity and field invariance of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]](b) and [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]; the class bookkeeping is that of [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]. before.title: Maxwell's equations in potential form: the Lorenz divergence, the decoupled wave equations and residual generators
before.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; the exact algebraic identities are stated with their pointwise-regularity hypotheses; solvability is left to the reachability theorem
before.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval, $c>0$, and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ ([[def-em-fields]]) and Lorenz divergence and wave operator $$G:=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi,\qquad W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta.$$ Let $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous sources ([[def-em-sources]]). (a) [Exact identities] Independently of any field equation, on $\Omega\times I$ $$\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+\nabla G.$$ Consequently the sourced Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold for $(E,B,\rho,J)$ if and only if $$W\varphi-\partial_tG=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad WA+\nabla G=\mu_0J\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$ (b) [Gauge shift] If $\chi$ is a gauge function of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$, then $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G-W\chi$ on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]), and the transformed pair has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). Hence $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge if and only if $W\chi=G$ on $\Omega\times I$. (c) [Decoupling] For this pair and sources, the pair is in Lorenz gauge and satisfies the two decoupled sourced wave equations $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and $WA=\mu_0J$ if and only if its field pair solves the sourced Maxwell system on $\Omega\times I$ (the source-free pair $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ being automatic for a potential pair). Thus in Lorenz gauge the sourced Maxwell system is exactly a pair of decoupled wave equations, componentwise for $A$. (d) [Residual generators] If $W\chi=0$ then the transform of a pair in Lorenz gauge is again in Lorenz gauge with the same field pair; the Lorenz condition therefore does not determine the potential pair. (e) [Scope] The identities and equivalences are properties of a given potential representation of class $C^2$; they assert no existence of a generator with $W\chi=G$ (or with prescribed data), which is the subject of the gauge-reachability theorem on this page, and they impose no boundary, decay or initial condition. A pair of class $C^1$ defines $E,B$ but need not have the second derivatives appearing in $W\varphi$, $WA$, $\Delta$ or $\partial_tG$, so $C^2$ is the exact standing regularity here.

abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A$ for the $C^2$ field $A$ ([[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]]), the definition $\Delta\varphi=\operatorname{div}
abla\varphi$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]) and the equality of mixed partials of the $C^2$ functions $\varphi,A$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]): $\operatorname{div}E=-\Delta\varphi-\partial_t\operatorname{div}A=W\varphi-\partial_tG$, and $\operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=
abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=WA+

full_object.statement:
Let $c>0$ and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$ be open. A **scalar-vector potential pair** of class $C^k$ on $\Omega$ (for an integer $k\ge0$) is a pair $(\varphi,A)$ with $\varphi:\Omega	o\mathbb R$ and $A:\Omega	o\mathbb R^3$ each of class $C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] (the components of $A$ componentwise). For such a pair with $k\ge1$ its **electric field** and **magnetic field** are $$E(\varphi,A):=-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA,\qquad B(\varphi,A):=\operatorname{curl}A,$$ where $
abla$ is the gradient of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]], $\partial_t$ is the partial derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] and $\operatorname{curl}$ and $\operatorname{div}$ are those of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]; both $E(\varphi,A)$ and $B(\varphi,A)$ are maps $\Omega	o\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^{k-1}$. For $k\ge1$ the **Lorenz divergence** of the pair is the function $$G(\varphi,A):=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi,$$ also of class $C^{k-1}$, and the pair is **in Lorenz gauge** on $\Omega$ when $G(\varphi,A)=0$ throughout $\Omega$. For $k\ge2$ and a $C^k$ function $\chi:\Omega	o\mathbb R$ (a **gauge function**) the **gauge transform** of the pair is $$T_{\chi}(\varphi,A):=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,\ A+
abla\chi),$$ again a potential pair, of class $C^{k-1}$. Finally, for a $C^2$ function $u:\Omega	o\mathbb R$ put $$Wu:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2u-\Delta u,$$ with $\Delta$ the Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]] and $\partial_t^2$ the second partial derivative in $t$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]); this is the normalization $W=c^{-2}\Box_c$ of the wave operator of speed $c$ of [[def-wave-equation-cauchy-data-and-wave-speed]]. For a $C^2$ map $U:\Omega	o\mathbb R^m$ with components $U_1,\dots,U_m$, one writes $WU:=(WU_1,\dots,WU_m)$ componentwise. Nothing in this definition asserts that a gauge function with prescribed auxiliary data exists, that every potential pair is gauge equivalent to a pair in Lorenz gauge, or that $Wu=g$ is solvable: those are conclusions with their own hypotheses. The signs $-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $A+
abla\chi$, the factor $c^{-2}$ in $G$ and the spelling *Lorenz* are part of the convention.

full_object.title: The microscopic vacuum Maxwell equations: smooth and weak branches
full_object.statement:
Adopt as a physical postulate of this framework the following four equations for the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous, and let $\rho,J$ be continuous. Then, with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

(b) [Weak branch] Let instead $E,B$ be locally integrable $\mathbb R^3$-valued fields and $\rho,J$ locally integrable scalar and vector fields on $I\times\Omega$, identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Let $\operatorname{div}$, $\operatorname{curl}$ and $\partial_t$ act as distributional derivatives, and let $\psi$ range over $C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]). Then the same four identities hold in the sense of [[def-distribution]]: the pairings $\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle$ and $\langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$ vanish for every such $\psi$, all derivatives being distributional derivatives ([[def-distributional-derivative]]). (c) [Scope] The postulate contains no magnetic charge: $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and no magnetic-source term appears in $\operatorname{curl}E$. Sources that are not locally integrable functions (point or sheet sources) are covered by neither branch and require their own definition. The equations are adopted classical vacuum physics in the named inertial chart; they are not deduced from charge conservation, from empirical agreement or from the special-relativity postulates, and this item by itself asserts no covariance under changes of inertial frame.
full_object.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. Obligations and conventions: the fields and sources are those of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], the operators are the published divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and the weak reading uses exactly the regular-distribution embedding, the test space and the distributional derivative named in the statement. The exposition must state that the four equations are adopted, that the choice of the sign and constant conventions is the one fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]], and that no magnetic charge is included; the sources not covered by either branch are excluded explicitly. Empirical support for Maxwell's equations is a nonlogical relation of the framework, not a proof, and no verification is claimed here.

Fix a smooth time-independent Dirichlet datum $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$. Then there is a gauge function $\psi$, of class $C^\infty$ on a neighbourhood of $\bar\Omega\times\bar I$, with $\psi(\cdot,t)|_{\partial\Omega}=g$ for every $t\in I$, such that $$\operatorname{div}(A+\nabla\psi)(\cdot,t)=0\qquad\text{on }\Omega\text{ for every }t\in I;$$ the transformed pair $T_\psi(\varphi,A)$ is in Coulomb gauge on $\Omega\times I$ and has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). before_object.statement: Let $c>0$, let $k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, $\omega:=c|k|$, and let $$\chi(x,t):=\cos(k\cdot x-\omega t),$$ the real part of the complex plane wave $e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)}$ of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] with wave vector $k$ and frequency $\omega=c|k|$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then $\chi$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ and $W\chi=0$, where $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ ([[def-wave-equation-cauchy-data-and-wave-speed]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]); indeed $\partial_t^2\chi=-\omega^2\chi$, $\Delta\chi=-|k|^2\chi$ and $\omega^2=c^2|k|^2$, so $W\chi=c^{-2}(-c^2|k|^2\chi)+|k|^2\chi=0$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). Consequently, for every potential pair $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^2$ jointly on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]), the gauge-transformed pair satisfies $$G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G(\varphi,A)\qquad\text{and}\qquad E(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=E(\varphi,A),\quad B(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=B(\varphi,A)$$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ ([[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]], [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]], [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]); in particular, if $(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge then $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge with the same field pair. Explicitly $\partial_t\chi=\omega\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$ and $\nabla\chi=-k\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$, so $\varphi'=\varphi-\omega\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$, $A'=A-k\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$; the zero pair is in Lorenz gauge and its transform $(-\omega\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t),\ -k\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t))$ is a nonzero pair that remains in Lorenz gauge and still represents the zero field pair. Thus the Lorenz condition does not determine the potential pair. The example is the residual generator $W\chi=0$ of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]] on the free-space branch; on a bounded domain with prescribed gauge boundary data the admissible generators are restricted, and no such data-dependent claim is made here.
before_object.strategy: Compute with the chain and product rules: $\partial_t\chi=\omega\sin\theta$, $\partial_t^2\chi=-\omega^2\cos\theta$, $\nabla\chi=-k\sin\theta$ and $\Delta\chi=-|k|^2\cos\theta$ at $\theta=k\cdot x-\omega t$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Substitute $\omega^2=c^2|k|^2$ to get $W\chi=0$. Then use the gauge-shift identity and field invariance of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]](b) and [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]; the class bookkeeping is that of [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]. No choice principle is used and no boundary condition is imposed, matching the free-space branch of the gauge-reachability statement on this page.
